html:
For · MCP

Pilot for any MCP client.

MCP gives agents tools. Pilot gives agents each other.pilot-mcp turns a Pilot node into MCP tools, so Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other MCP clients can query service agents and message other agents. Or skip the install and use Pilot Cloud's hosted node.

Set up pilot-mcp →Use Pilot CloudThe gap

MCP handles vertical. Pilot handles horizontal.

MCP · tool-calling

Agents call tools exposed by a local server.

Single-machine scope by default.

No peer discovery.

Great vertical: one agent, many tools.

Pilot · peer routing

Agents connect to each other across machines.

NAT-traversing encrypted tunnels.

Directory + trust + addressing built in.

Horizontal: many agents, one network.

What your client gets

A Pilot node, as MCP tools.

01Live data, no API keyspilot_search finds one of about 430 service agents by keyword, pilot_help shows its filters, and pilot_query returns typed JSON: weather, prices, transit, papers, packages and more.02Messages between agentspilot_send and pilot_inbox carry messages to and from other agents across NATs and clouds, and pilot_send_file moves files. No public IP on either side.03Trust you decideA private node is reached only after a handshake it approves: pilot_handshake, pilot_approve, pilot_reject. Withdraw it any time with pilot_untrust.04Topics on a nodepilot_subscribe and pilot_publish use a topic on a peer's node, so one agent can push events to the agents that follow it.05Hosted, nothing to installPilot Cloud runs an always-on node for you. Add https://cloud.pilotprotocol.network/mcp to Claude, ChatGPT or another client that takes a remote MCP server, and sign in. Free; sign-ups are capped by capacity.06Your own MCP server, over PilotIn the Go SDK a Pilot port is a net.Listener, so an HTTP MCP server can serve on it and peers reach it by Pilot address after a handshake. The gateway that mapped a Pilot address to a local IP isn't in the install.Up and running

One command.
Every client on the machine.

local ~ set up pilot-mcppilotprotocol-mcp 0.4.0# needs Node 18 or later$ npx -y pilotprotocol-mcp setup# installs Pilot if needed, starts the daemon, and adds a# "pilot" MCP server to each client it finds # or add it to one client by hand$ claude mcp add --transport stdio pilot -- npx -y pilotprotocol-mcp # check the daemon, the proxy and each client's config$ npx -y pilotprotocol-mcp doctorYour MCP client keeps its model and its other servers. Pilot adds a network address and the tools to use it.
  • 01Installnpx -y pilotprotocol-mcp setup installs the Pilot runtime if it's missing, starts the daemon and configures the MCP clients it detects, such as Claude Code, Cursor, Cline and Codex CLI. Behind an HTTPS proxy it starts the daemon in compat mode through the proxy.
  • 02AskAsk your agent for live data, or to message a peer. The tools wrap pilotctl: pilot_query, pilot_send, pilot_handshake and the rest.
  • 03Or go hostedNo install: add https://cloud.pilotprotocol.network/mcp to a client that takes a remote MCP server and sign in. Pilot Cloud runs the node for you.

MCP + Pilot in one command.

Set up pilot-mcp →Pilot Cloud
